scholarships.title: DAAD Helmut-Schmidt-Programme (Master's Scholarships for Public Policy and Good Governance - PPGG)

existing.funding_period: for the full duration of the funded master's course
existing.description: The DAAD Helmut-Schmidt-Programme, also known as Public Policy and Good Governance, is funded by the German Federal Foreign Office and supports future leaders from developing and emerging countries who want to promote democracy and social justice in their home regions. It funds places on selected English-taught master's courses in public policy, good governance, international relations, public management, public administration, civil society, geo-governance, peace and conflict studies, and development and socio-economic policy at seven German higher education institutions. Applications go directly to the participating universities rather than to the DAAD, and the published application window is 1 June to 31 July each year, with the 2027-intake round closed on 31 July 2026.
eligibility: Very well qualified graduate with a first university degree (Bachelor or equivalent)
National of or normally resident in a developing or emerging country on the DAAD list of eligible countries
Wants to actively contribute to the social and economic development of their home country or region
Both young graduates without professional experience and mid-career professionals may apply
First academic degree in political science, law, economics or administration, or a related field relevant to social, political and economic development
Must have completed the first degree by the closing date of the application round
Academic admission to the chosen master's course at one of the participating institutions
existing.eligibility_summary: Very well qualified graduates with a first university degree (Bachelor or equivalent) from a developing or emerging country, both young graduates without professional experience and mid-career professionals, who want to contribute to the social and economic development of their home country or region.
benefits: Full scholarship for one of the selected master's courses at a participating German institution
German language course in Germany lasting up to six months before the master's studies
Special tutoring at the host institution and study in small groups
Networking events across courses and tailor-made workshops
coverage: Full scholarship for the selected master's course at a participating German university
German language course in Germany of up to six months before starting the master's studies
Scholarship holders study in small groups with special tutoring at the host institution
Networking events across courses and tailor-made workshops
requirements: Apply directly to the master's course or courses at the participating universities, and not to the DAAD
The application period for all participating institutions is 1 June to 31 July each year
Graduation must be completed by the end of the application round, since the DAAD FAQ states that candidates who will not graduate until 31 July cannot be admitted to that application round
Applications may be sent to a maximum of two of the participating universities, with priorities for first and second choice
The application and the scholarship are applied for together through the university's own procedure
Study the chosen master's course in Germany after the German language course
documents: DAAD application form for Research Grant and Study Scholarships
Documents required by the chosen master's course, as specified by that university
The application must be submitted to the master's course of your choice, not to the DAAD
existing.english_requirement: The participating master's courses have an international orientation and are taught in English. Before taking up the master's studies, scholarship holders take part in a German language course in Germany lasting up to six months.
application_method: Direct application to the selected participating university or universities using their own application portal, including the DAAD application form
existing.selection_notes: Applications are submitted to the universities, which shortlist candidates for the DAAD scholarship. The current call's detailed selection procedure, interview arrangements and decision dates are set out in the current-call announcement PDF, which could not be extracted as text.
existing.best_fit: Graduates with a first degree from a developing or emerging country who want a career in public policy, governance, public administration, law, economics or development, and who can meet the admission requirements of one of the seven participating institutions.
existing.notes: Participating institutions and courses listed by the DAAD: University of Applied Sciences Bonn-Rhein-Sieg (Social Protection); University of Duisburg-Essen (Development and Governance); Erfurt School of Public Policy at the University of Erfurt (Public Policy); University of Magdeburg (Peace and Conflict Studies); Osnabrueck University of Applied Sciences (Management in Nonprofit Organisations); University of Passau (Development Studies); University of Passau (Governance and Public Policy). Note that the DAAD has reduced the network from the eight institutions of earlier years to seven for the current call, so the list must be re-checked each year.
existing.duration: Duration of the selected master's course, normally two years; preceded by a German language course in Germany of up to six months
existing.application_period: 1 June to 31 July each year, applied for directly at the participating universities. The 2027-intake round closed on 31 July 2026, before the verification date.
existing.deadline_display: "The application period for all seven higher education institutions is from 1 June until 31 July 2026", with the application deadline being 31 July each year
existing.program_type: Full master's scholarship for public policy and governance studies at selected German universities
